Allow viewers to request live updates
Your location is encrypted on your phone. Only the people you choose can decrypt it.
It travels through relays: independent servers run by volunteers or companies (you can pick your own). Relays cannot see your location, your name or your contacts\' names.
Your contacts may use relays other than yours. Before your phone connects to one of those, the app asks you, because whoever runs it would see your internet address.

Relays that follow the rules keep only your latest encrypted position, and delete it 15 minutes after it was sent. A relay that breaks the rules, or anyone else, could keep copies. They stay encrypted, and the phones delete the keys that could open them within about a day.

Your location is never sent while you are not sharing. While the app is open and you have contacts, it asks the relays whether anyone is sharing with you. People you stop sharing with cannot read anything you send afterwards.
You are not sharing your location.
